Enforced by revert to lz-tdd@0.0.2 rather than by prose, and the two guards that MANDATED content in those files were removed because a guard enforcing an out-of-scope change is itself out of scope.

decisions.decision: Roster entries must be STRING LITERALS, not label constants.
decisions.rationale: The audit's own fix for the rename blind spot was to add a label constant to NEW_LABELS, but the emission site pushes the same constant, so a rename moves both sides and the leg stays green -- a guard that cannot fail, reintroduced by the fix meant to close it. Verified independently at :540, :615 and :935 before overriding the audit. 8 of 13 entries remain constant-derived and are recorded as rename-blind.

decisions.decision: Findings 11a-c were STRENGTHENED rather than relabelled.
decisions.rationale: The brief permitted weakening a label where closing the gap was disproportionate, but measured content made a sharper needle cheaper than a label edit in all three cases -- a row's first cell, a numbered step, a section heading. Only naming.md's label was retitled, because the enforced heading says codebase's rather than house.

decisions.decision: Scope-removal labels stay OUT of RETIRED_LABELS.
decisions.rationale: That roster records this task's taxonomy retirements so the gate can tell a deliberate retirement from an accidental drop. Folding in a scope removal would blur two different reasons a guard can be absent and dilute the roster's only real value.

decisions.decision: Post-plan corrections use commit prefixes OUTSIDE the (test|fix|refactor|docs)(quick-260729-lc9) family.

A seventh under those types would break the plan's own ceiling, so revert(...), fix(instrument):, docs(instrument):, refactor(beck-ref): were used instead. context_notes: THE SESSION'S REAL LESSON IS ABOUT WHERE DEFECTS HIDE, NOT ABOUT THE TAXONOMY. Six consecutive rounds each introduced a NEW self-falsifying claim INSIDE the previous round's repair, and the last two instances came from the REVIEW machinery itself: the plan-checker's proposed fix for BLOCKER-B could never have passed (check() prints the offender string only on failure, so pinning it in the output was unsatisfiable on a green run), and the audit's proposed fix for the rename blind spot asserted nothing (constant on both sides of the comparison). Both were caught by the agent RECEIVING the fix rather than the one proposing it, which is the argument for keeping propose and apply adversarially split instead of collapsing them into one agent. SECOND LESSON: mechanism review and content review find DISJOINT defects. Five plan-check iterations audited legs, guards, counts and exit codes, and passed prose that an unprimed reviewer immediately called BROKEN -- lz-tpp's rule defined only one side of a two-sided distinction, in the skill where the undefined side is the likelier reading. No amount of leg-counting finds that, and no amount of prose review finds a fail-open || echo 0. Run both. THIRD: BLOCKER-A was caused by measuring a guard against its REGEX instead of the code that RUNS it -- the FILES matcher splits on newlines and tests per line, so a newline-bearing needle could never match, and the guard would have deadlocked Tasks 3 and 4 forever while looking correct in isolation. Read the evaluator. MY OWN ERRORS, all caught and all the same shape -- asserting something without checking the thing it names: I passed the planner's pre-patch line count (1591) into an executor brief after my own edits took it to 1635, harmless only because the base SHA matched and the executor flagged it; I removed the SEAM-02 guard and left its claim standing in the GREEN SUMMARY, which is the exact class the plan had a dedicated leg for, missed because the hand-edit sat outside the plan's leg coverage; and I over-read an owner answer, stating the Fowler fix would be re-applied when the option chosen covered only the path retarget. WHAT WENT RIGHT AND SHOULD BE REPEATED: incremental output-file writes saved three agents from spend-limit and classifier kills with zero loss; an executor blocked by the classifier chose to land NOTHING rather than leave unproven edits, and its clean tree plus written design cost nothing to resume; and every agent that disagreed with its brief on the merits was right to, including when it contradicted me.
